validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE confirmed at high tier: this is a real BP subsea gas tie-back in the North Damietta offshore concession, East Nile Delta. Independently corroborated by four non-GEM sources that all describe the same physical fact pattern — a one-well subsea development at Qattameya tied back via a new ~50km pipeline to the existing Ha'py/Tuart field facilities: globalshift.co.uk (Oct 2020 news entry: 'BP (100%) announced the start of gas production from the Qattameya gas field in the North Damietta concession in 108m of water... developed through a one-well subsea development and tie-back to the Ha'py and Tuart field development via a new 50km pipeline'; also has an independent March 2017 discovery-well entry for the same field, 'Qattameya Shallow-1'), egyptoil-gas.com news article ('BP Begins Production From Qattameya Field') giving start date Oct 26 2020, capacity 'about 50 million cubic feet of natural gas per day (mmcf/d)', and 'tied to the Ha'py and Tuart fields through a 50 kilometer (km) pipeline', and offshore-technology.com's project page ('developed with one subsea well tied-back to Eni's Ha'py and Taurt field facilities through a new 50km-long pipeline... expected to produce up to 50 million metric standard cubic feet per day'). Status=operating, Fuel=Gas, StartYear1=2020, Capacity=50.00 MMcf/d, FuelSource='Qattameya Gas Field' all check out against this independent reporting. Location also checked: the Arabic almalnews.com article (current Location [ref]) verifies live and names Qattameya ('قطامية') explicitly (url_verifier OK on that token) — StartLocation/EndLocation ('North Damietta offshore concession' / 'Hapy&Tuart Gas Field facilities') match the same industry description. Capacity is single-sourced (medium tier per rubric) but the number is stated identically across two of the four sources (egyptoil-gas, offshore-technology), so it is not in doubt even though only one is cited. Note: a prior route-creation pass (RouteCreator=CB, RouteNotes on this row) already independently verified the same underlying facts via bp.com, mees.com and pipeline-journal.net, and additionally established the tie-in point is specifically the Ha'py platform (Tuart is itself a subsea-only satellite tied to Ha'py by a separate ~70km line) — consistent with everything found here.

CLASSIFICATION concern. All four independent sources that actually describe this pipeline call it a single-well SUBSEA TIE-BACK, never a transmission line: globalshift.co.uk ('a one-well subsea development and tie-back... via a new 50km pipeline'), egyptoil-gas.com ('developed as a one-well subsea development and tie-back to existing infrastructure'), offshore-technology.com ('developed with one subsea well tied-back to Eni's Ha'py and Taurt field facilities... a 50km-long umbilical'), and pipeline-journal.net ('tied back to the Ha'py and Tuart field development'). This is a production gathering/tie-back flowline linking one new subsea well to nearby existing field-processing facilities — not a cross-country or national-grid transmission trunk, and 'gathering' is a valid PipelineType per controlled_vocab.md. Corroborating evidence from the OPPOSITE direction: the current PipelineType [ref] (EGAS Annual Report 2018-2019, the 'Highlights and Targets' edition hosted at egyptoil-gas.com) contains an explicit, itemized 'NATIONAL GAS GRID PIPELINES COMPLETED' and '...UNDER [CONSTRUCTION]' list with named lines and diameters (e.g. 'Algameel/Damietta pipeline 50km-42"', 'Tina/Abu Sultan pipeline 92km-42"') — i.e. this is precisely the kind of document that WOULD list Qattameya-Tuart if it were a national-grid transmission asset, and it is absent from that list. Full-text search of the PDF for 'Qattameya', 'Tuart', and 'Hapy'/"Ha'py" returns zero hits (confirmed both via pdftotext and via url_verifier, which FAILs this URL against the token 'Qattameya'). I also checked whether this could be one of the scope's 'identified visually off the p.35 map' rows per the standing caveat for this cohort — it is not: this particular PDF (the 2018/2019 'Highlights and Targets' edition, 36 pages) has no national pipeline grid map at all; PDF page 35 is a section-title cover page ('HIGHLIGHTS AND TARGETS 2018/2019'), confirmed by rendering it to an image. So the citation is a plain mis-cite, not an unindexed map reference — the source document never engages with this pipeline in text OR image form.

validity.recommendation: re-cite Length [ref] away from the EGAS Annual Report PDF (value is fine, citation is not)
validity.researcher_notes: The LengthKnown value (50.00 km) is well corroborated — all four independent sources agree on '50km' for this pipeline. But the citation currently attached to Length [ref] (EGAS Annual Report 2018-2019 PDF) does not mention Qattameya, Tuart, or Ha'py anywhere (see the classification finding above — zero full-text hits, url_verifier FAIL on the token 'Qattameya', and no map in this PDF edition). This is a mis-citation, not a wrong value: the number is right, the source pointer is not. Recommend swapping Length [ref] to offshore-technology.com and/or pipeline-journal.net, both of which state the 50km figure directly and both pass url_verifier.

validity.recommendation: verify or blank Diameter (24 in) — currently unsupported by any source that discusses this pipeline
validity.researcher_notes: Diameter=24in / DiameterUnits=in is cited to the same EGAS Annual Report PDF that never mentions this pipeline (see above — confirmed dead citation). Unlike Length, I could not independently confirm the diameter value at all: none of the four sources describing this exact tie-back (globalshift.co.uk, egyptoil-gas.com, offshore-technology.com, pipeline-journal.net) states a pipe diameter. offshore-technology.com additionally calls the connection 'a 50km-long umbilical' alongside the pipeline description, consistent with a small-bore single-well subsea tie-back system rather than a large 24in trunk line — a 24in diameter would be unusually large for a one-well subsea tieback of this kind, which raises further doubt the figure is real rather than copied from an unrelated line in the source PDF (which does contain several real 24in-labeled lines elsewhere, e.g. 'Project Rehabilitation gas supply pipeline 24"', none of which are this pipeline). Not fabricating a replacement value per the standing rule against inventing specs on weak fields — recommend leaving Diameter blank (or noting it as inferred/unsourced in ResearcherNotes) until a document that actually names Qattameya/Ha'py/Tuart gives a pipe size.

summary: P8025 confirmed real and well-sourced (4 independent industry sources) but likely MISCLASSIFIED as transmission when every source describes a single-well subsea gathering tie-back — recommend 'gathering'; Length citation is dead (EGAS PDF never mentions this pipeline) though the 50km value itself is fine; Diameter (24in) is unsupported by any source and should be verified or blanked; filled blank StartMonth1=10 (October 2020).
